title: A Learnable Meta - USA State Highway Markers

cards.note: The Alabama Highway Sign can be somewhat easily recognized as it just has the shape of the state.
The Alaska Highway Sign can be easily recognized by the stars on the sign resembling the stars on the flag, as well as the word "Alaska" being written on top of the Sign.
The Arizona Highway Sign can be easily recognized by the shape of the state being printed on the sign, as well as the word "Arizona" being at the top of the sign.
The Arkansas Highway Sign is somewhat easy recognizable by the shape of the state being printed on the Sign.
The California Highway Sign is very easy recognizable by the distinct green colour and shape as well as having "California" written on top of the sign.
The Colorado Highway Sign is very easily recognizable as its the only Highway Sign to have the State Flag on top of it.

The Connecticut Highway Sign only consists of a white Sign with the Roadnumber.

NOTE: -the same sign can be found in Maine, Massachusetts and West Virginia

The Delaware Highway Sign consists of a white Circle on a black sign.

NOTE: similiar signs can be found in Iowa, Mississippi, New Mexico (on Special Occasion) and New Jersey
The Florida Highway Sign can easily be recognized by the shape of the state being printed on the sign as well as the name "Florida" being on top of the sign.
The Georgia Highway Sign can be recognized by the shape of the state being printed on the sign.

The Hawaii Highway Sign can be recognized by the shape on the sign.

Oregon and Virginia both have a similiar sign, but facing downwards.

The Idaho Highway Sign can easily be recognized by the shape of the state being printed on top of the sign as well as the name "Idaho" on the bottom of the sign.

Also half the sign is black, so it's easily recognizable from a distance.
The Illinois Highway Sign only consists of a white plate with the name "Illinois" printed on top. Can be confused with Indiana which looks the same with "Indiana" being written on top.
The Indiana Highway Sign only consists of a white plate with the word "Indiana" written on top.

The Iowa Highway Sign consists of a white Circle on a black sign.

NOTE: similiar signs can be found in Delaware, Mississippi, New Mexico (on Special Occasion) and New Jersey
The Kansas Highway Sign can easily be recognized, as it's the only sign that consists of a yellow circle on top of a black sign.
The Kentucky Highway Sign can easily be confused with the Highway Signs that consist of the white circle on top of the black sign, but the Kentucky Sign has a more ovale shape and isn't a circle.
The Louisiana Highway Sign can easily be recognized by the shape of the state on the sign as well as the letters "LA" on top of the sign.

The Maine Highway Sign only consists of a white Sign with the Roadnumber.

NOTE: -the same sign can be found in Connecticut, Massachusetts and West Virginia
The Maryland Highway Sign can easily be recognized by the name "Maryland" on top of the Sign with a distinct black border and the road number underneath.

The Massachusetts Highway Sign only consists of a white Sign with the Roadnumber.

NOTE: -the same sign can be found in Connecticut, Maine and West Virginia

The Michigan Highway Sign can easily be recognized by the diamond shape on the black sign with a big black M at the top. NOTE: It can be confused with the North Carolina Sign, but that lacks the M at the top.
The Minnesota Highway Sign can easily be recognized by the blue colour and the name "Minnesota" being written on top.

The Mississippi Highway Sign consists of a white Circle on a black sign.

NOTE: similiar signs can be found in Delaware, Iowa, New Mexico (on Special Occasion) and New Jersey

The Missouri Highway Sign can be recognized by the shape of the state on the sign.

On supplementaral routes you will find a white sign, with a letter in black in the middle and a black outline. These are found on the map near other highways and are mapped with the respective letter.

The Montana Highway Sign can be recognized by the black frame and the name "Montana" on top of the sign.

On Secondary roads you will see a white shape resembling a tip of an arrow on a black sign.

The Nebraska Highway Sign can be recognized by the trapez shape and the name "Nebraska" on top of the sign, as well as a cart at the bottom.

On Secondary Roads, the sign will only show the trapez shape, not the state name on top, or the cart at the bottom.
The Nevada Highway Sign can be recognized by the shape of the state on the sign.
The New Hampshire Highway Sign can be recognized by the shape of the state on the sign.

The New Jersey Highway Sign consists of a white Circle on a black sign.

NOTE: similiar signs can be found in Delaware, Iowa, New Mexico (on Special Occasion) and Mississippi

New Mexico Highway Signs can be recognized by the white circle on a black sign with a thin red circle inside the white circle.

NOTE: -the red inner circle isn't always there

      -similiar signs can be found in Delaware, Iowa, Mississippi and New Jersey
The New York Highway Sign can be recognized by a hexagonal white shape on the black sign.

The North Carolina Highway Sign can be recognized by a white diamond shape on a black sign.

NOTE: Michigan has a similiar sign, but has a black M at the top of the diamond.
The North Dakote Highway Sign can be recognized by the shape of the state on the sign as well as the name "North Dakota" on top of the sign.
The Ohio Highway Sign can be recognized by the shape of the state on the sign.
The Oklahoma Highway Sign can be recognized by a thin outline of the state behind the road number.

The Oregon Highway Sign can be recognized by a missshaped circle on the black sign.

NOTE: the same sign can be found in Virginia, but the landscape is very different
The Pennsylvania Highway Sign can be recognized by a white trapez with a little extension on top.

The Rhode Island Highway Sign can be recognized by a white sign and the letters "RI" above the road number.

NOTE: a similiar sign can be found in Connecticut, Maine, Massachusetts and West Virginia, but in Rhode Island there will always be a "RI" at the top
The South Carolina Highway Sign can be recognized by a distinct blue Outline, blue road number and the name "South Carolina" as well as a little shape of the state on the sign.
The South Dakota Highway Sign can be recognized by the clear green Outline on the sign forming the shape of the state.

The Tennesse Highway Sign can be recognized by the shape of the state at the bottom and the name "Tennesse" written inside the shape.

On secondary roads, you will find a white triangle pointing downwards on a black sign instead.

The Texas Highway Sign can be recognized by a slightly thicker black outline and the name "Texas" written at the bottom.

On farm roads you will find a black sign with the shape of texas on top and the words "FARM ROAD" or "RANCH ROAD" written on the sign although these roads may be very hard to find.
The Utah Highway Signs can be recognized by the shape of a bee house on the sign.
The Vermont Highway Sign can be recognized by the green font and border on the sign as well as the name "Vermont" at the top.

The Virginia Highway Sign can be recognized by a misshaped white circle on a black sign.

On secondary roads, they use the same White circle on black backround design, like in Delaware, Iowa, Mississippi, New Jersey and Maine.

NOTE: -The same sign can be found in Oregon.
The Washington Highway Sign can be recognized by the white silhouette of George Washington's Head on the sign.

The West Virginia Highway Sign can be recognzied by a white sign, often with a black outline.

NOTE: The same sign can be found in Connecticut, Massachusetts and Maine.
The Wisconsin Highway Sign can be recognized by a rounded white rectangle with an extension on top and a little white triangle at the bottom.
The Wyoming Highway Sign can easily be recognized, as it's the only full yellow Highway Sign in the entire USA. In addition it has the name "Wyoming" written at the top.
